children.text: Five rungs from support to causal claims: smoke, golden logits, activation-reference checks, probes, interventions. Each rung is a different claim; "supported" means an execution path exists.
each rung is a different claim: "supported" means an execution path exists, it does not mean the row is
numerically validated. top-1 agreement is not logit equality; deterministic semantic output is not
timing reproducibility (docs/validation.md; the rungs the whole series cites).
GGUF file to loader to tensors to the reference path to logits, with hidden-state observation points on the reference path and a packed Q8 fast path that must agree within the recorded envelopes.
Baseline capture, altered run, patch one layer, downstream output changes, restore the original activation, output returns to baseline, the frozen restoration criterion is bit-exact.

The reference path expands the whole weight matrix to f32; the v0.3 path keeps packed blocks mmap-resident and runs native K-quant matvec.
Decode one block into a small per-thread buffer, multiply by the activation slice, accumulate; the whole matrix never becomes f32-resident.
not this: unpack the entire matrix to f32

per-thread workspace for the compressed path is ≤ 9 KiB and no model-scale f32 buffer is created

Conceptual super-block layout: Q4_K groups 8 blocks of 32 weights with per-block 2-bit scale factors and offsets; Q6_K groups 16 blocks of 16 weights with int8 scales; dispatch is per tensor because a Q4_K_M file mixes tensor dtypes.
dispatch is per tensor, not per file: a Q4_K_M checkpoint mixes dtypes, llama-3.2-1b q4_k_m contains
96 × Q4_K + 17 × Q6_K + 34 × F32 tensors (docs/v03-execution-contracts.md §5), so both native kernels must exist,
and the loader reads the inventory from the GGUF headers rather than trusting the file name.
